sources.citation: Van der Meer, Hans. 2008. Bau organized phonology data. Ms., 12 pp. Ukarumpa: SIL-PNG (SIL archives 31032).
sources.note: Describes BAU [bbd], the closest relative (Z'graggen 1971:26: high mutual intelligibility); 0 occurrences of 'Gumalu'. Bau rule pp. 7-8: monomorphemic words stress the first closed syllable, else the first syllable; polymorphemic words grammatically conditioned. Not a Gumalu source.
meds: Z'graggen 1980 and 1975, both 'wordlist_or_less'; no grammar, sketch or phonology exists for the language in Glottolog.

sources.note: Only source: Z'graggen (1980) lexicon; IPA re-keying with no stress marks.

sources.citation: OLAC, 'Resources in and about the Gumalu language' (Wayback capture, up-to-date as of 2025-11-03)
sources.note: Holdings: Rosetta Swadesh list (= Z'graggen 1980 forms), transnewguinea.org, Glottolog, Ethnologue. No SIL Language & Culture Archives item, no description of any kind.

sources.citation: Roberts, John R. 1991. A study of the dialects of Amele. Language and Linguistics in Melanesia 22: 67-126.
sources.note: Uses Gumalu forms taken from Z'graggen 1980 in consonant-correspondence Tables 13-17 (fn. 7); nothing on Gumalu stress (its stress remarks concern Amele).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. xvi+184+10 pp. (Gumalu = language C6)
sources.note: Intro sec. 6 (p. viii): 'The transcription is semi-phonemic; i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted...'. The word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the volume; the 101 Gumalu (C6) rows carry no stress marks. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Gazetteer: C6 Gumalu, pop. 271, village Gumalu (155). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study Vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Classification only: Gum Family = Sihan, Gumalu, Isebe, Amele, Bau, Panim (2.8.2.2.1.2.3); C6 Gumalu pop. 271; comparative pronoun tables. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 1.3.3, p. 6 (survey-wide, all languages): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Sec. 2.21.11.14, p. 26: Gumalu GUM (330) first listed by Z'graggen 1969:40 as Bau-speaking, then accepted as distinct with 'a high degree of mutual intelligibility'; 'Gumalu Language is also included into the population figures but not into the description of typological features in the remainder of this study'. No Gumalu phonology at all.
